paper_metadata.title: Antiepileptic drugs withdrawal in patients with idiopathic generalized epilepsy

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses consecutive recruitment from referral centers and provides clear inclusion/exclusion criteria. However, it excludes 'non-responders' and those with missing data, which may introduce selection bias by only including patients with better follow-up adherence or clearer clinical profiles.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: two regional referral University hospitals: Institute for Child and Adolescents Health Care in Novi Sad and Clinic for Neurology and Psychiatry for Children and Youth in Belgrade, Serbia
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly defined as pediatric/adolescent patients from two specific tertiary centers.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Subjects were identified among consecutive patients from two regional referral University hospitals
items.reasoning: Consecutive sampling is a robust method to minimize selection bias.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: The study was conducted from June 2001 through December 2009.
items.reasoning: The dates are explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Institute for Child and Adolescents Health Care in Novi Sad and Clinic for Neurology and Psychiatry for Children and Youth in Belgrade, Serbia (85 km apart from each other).
items.reasoning: Specific institutions and geographic locations are provided.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Inclusion criteria were: diagnosis of IGE according to the ILAE criteria, established clinical remission of at least two years before AED withdrawal and clinical follow up for at least two years after withdrawal or until seizure relapse.
items.reasoning: Criteria include diagnostic standards, 'zero time' (remission duration), and follow-up requirements.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Patients who dropped out of the follow up from different reasons – non-responders or attending other Clinics were not included.
items.reasoning: The exclusion of 'non-responders' suggests that the final sample might not represent the full spectrum of eligible patients, potentially biasing results toward those more likely to succeed or remain in care.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The following variables, derived from the case records were analyzed: aside from the basic demographic ones (age and sex), age at seizure onset, type of seizure, cognitive and neurological status...
items.reasoning: Table 3 and the text provide a comprehensive list of baseline clinical and demographic factors.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the study requires a 2-year follow-up for inclusion, it explicitly excludes patients who dropped out or had missing data. This 'complete case' approach masks the true attrition rate and fails to analyze if those lost to follow-up differed from those who completed the study.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Patients who dropped out of the follow up from different reasons – non-responders or attending other Clinics were not included.
items.reasoning: The total number of eligible patients versus those included is not stated, making it impossible to calculate the response rate.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: There is no mention of attempts to trace or contact patients who were lost to follow-up.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: non-responders or attending other Clinics
items.reasoning: General reasons are given, but not quantified or analyzed for impact.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: No data is provided regarding the characteristics of the excluded drop-outs.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: Because the drop-outs were not described, a comparison is impossible.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors (syndrome type, EEG features) are well-defined and measured using standardized clinical and electrophysiological methods (ILAE criteria, 10-20 EEG system).

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: diagnosis of IGE according to the ILAE criteria... EEG records were classified, as abnormal if EEG included unequivocal epileptiform abnormalities
items.reasoning: Syndromes and EEG worsening are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: EEG in both settings was recorded according to the international 10–20 electrode placement system (21 channel) using Oxford Medilec EEG machine.
items.reasoning: Standardized international systems were used for measurement.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Age at seizure onset above 10 years... Age of AED withdrawal above 15 years.
items.reasoning: Cut-points are used for age, but it is not explicitly stated if these were pre-specified or data-driven (though they align with clinical norms).

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: EEG in both settings was recorded according to the international 10–20 electrode placement system
items.reasoning: The protocol was consistent across the two centers.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: Patients who met all inclusion criteria were identified... all needed relevant data were available from the case history notes.
items.reasoning: The study only included those with complete records.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: Imputation was not used; missing data resulted in exclusion.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure relapse) is a clear clinical event, and the study used a standardized follow-up period and clinical evaluation to capture it.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: The primary outcome end-point was seizure recurrences after the AED discontinuation.
items.reasoning: The outcome is clearly defined as clinical seizure recurrence.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Subjects as outpatients were seen by neurologists and/or neuropediatricians/epileptologists in the follow up intervals of 3–6 months
items.reasoning: Outcomes were verified by specialist clinical examination.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: follow up intervals of 3–6 months, until the end of studied period.
items.reasoning: The follow-up schedule was standardized for the cohort.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Outcome Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Outcome of interest is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study accounts for several confounders in a multivariable model. However, the sample size (n=44 for the final analysis) is quite small for a Cox regression with multiple variables, which may limit the stability and reliability of the adjustment.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: The following variables... were analyzed: aside from the basic demographic ones (age and sex), age at seizure onset, type of seizure, cognitive and neurological status, history of status epilepticus, EEGs...
items.reasoning: A wide range of clinical and demographic confounders were captured.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: The AED therapy duration was in range 1–9 years (median 4). The length of stable clinical remission while on AED was in range 2.5–9 years (median 4).
items.reasoning: Treatment-related confounders are quantified.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: derived from the case records
items.reasoning: Data were extracted from medical records, which is standard for this study type.

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: These variables entered computerized database formed for all out-patients regularly examined.
items.reasoning: A uniform database was used for all participants.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods are used if imputation is used for missing confounder data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: Missing data led to exclusion rather than imputation.

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: No matching or stratification was used in the design phase.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: Relative risks for recurrence during the follow-up were investigated by Cox regression analysis – uni/ multivariate analyses
items.reasoning: Multivariable Cox regression was used to adjust for confounders.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Confounding Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Important potential confounders are appropriately accounted for, limiting potential bias with respect to the relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods are appropriate (Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression). However, the exclusion of 15 patients who had 'EEG worsening' but no seizures from the relapse analysis is a significant methodological choice that could influence the reported risk ratios.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: time to seizure relapse was analyzed by Kaplan Meir method... Factors of possible prognostic values were evaluated by x2 test. Relative risks... investigated by Cox regression
items.reasoning: The strategy is clearly outlined.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: In multivariate analysis, retained significant factors were: seizure types and EEG worsening.
items.reasoning: The study uses a significance-based approach for model building, which can sometimes lead to overfitting, especially with small samples.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: Cox regression analysis – uni/ multivariate analyses to allow for variable length of follow up.
items.reasoning: Cox regression is the standard for time-to-event data with variable follow-up.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: This group of patients, therefore, was excluded from the estimation of risk for seizure recurrence.
items.reasoning: While transparently reported, the exclusion of patients who had treatment reintroduced based on EEG alone (without waiting for clinical relapse) effectively censors a high-risk group, potentially underestimating the true relapse risk.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Statistical Analysis and Presentation Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: The statistical analysis is appropriate for the design of the study, limiting potential for presentation of invalid or spurious results.
